title: Fragment Sentinels for Streaming Structured Output and SDK Compatibility Shim
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a sentinel-based fragment protocol + compatibility shim for older SDKs to make streaming structured JSON robust against mid-stream truncation, nested tool/function-call boundaries, and escape ambiguity. This ticket proposes: (1) a tiny in-stream sentinel envelope that marks fragment start/finish with fragment-id, byte-offset, and checksum; (2) a deterministic escaping map so sentinels never collide with user payloads; (3) a final 'manifest' event for legacy SDKs that don't support incremental fragment assembly; (4) idempotent replay and retry semantics tied to fragment ids so clients can resume from the last confirmed fragment without double-applying tool calls. Goals: reduce failed structured-output decoding by 90% for truncated or retried streams, ensure tool/function-call boundaries remain consistent on resume, and add a short-term compat mode for older SDKs while new SDKs adopt in-band fragments.
acceptance_criteria: Server emits fragment sentinel envelope for every top-level structured chunk with fields: frag_id, start_offset, end_offset, checksum, meta (string)
Deterministic escaping map introduced in runtime and SDKs; tests cover edgecases with control characters and model-inserted sentinel text

Compatibility shim: when header X-Redwood-Compat: legacy_manifest=true is present, server emits final manifest describing frag_id -> byte ranges; older SDKs can reassemble without changing chunk parsing
Tool/function-call boundaries are preserved across retries: retries must be idempotent and not replay tool invocations already acknowledged by the client
SLO: structured-output decode error rate reduced by >=90% on simulated network truncation tests
Integration tests and e2e QA pass on internal canary region; PRs merged and release notes drafted
notes_and_decisions: 2026-02-11 - Proposal: use ASCII sentinel string '<SEG:FRAG>' with a canonical escape '\u003cSEG:FRAG\u003e' in payloads. Tradeoff: longer sentinel vs simpler matching. Chosen for human readability in logs.
2026-02-16 - Decision: embed minimal metadata (frag_id, seq_start, seq_end, crc32) to keep per-event payload small and minimize RTT impact on streaming clients.

2026-02-20 - Trade-off discussion: two approaches considered — (A) full-semantic checkpoints (heavy, but model-aware) vs (B) byte-fragment sentinels (lightweight). We picked (B) for first iteration to ship quickly and enable a measured rollout.
2026-02-24 - PM review (Jasmin O'Leary): ensure compatibility header is well-documented and off by default. PM requested analytics event for legacy-manifest usage.
2026-02-26 - Design feedback (Priya Nair): UX for streamed JSON in Console should surface fragment gaps and show resume point. Added acceptance criteria for console visualization later-phase.
2026-03-01 - Security review note: no secret data stored in fragment metadata; CRC only. Security accepted low risk; flagging for final review before GA.
implementation_plan: Server: implement sentinel emitter in runtime output layer (cpp/serve/runtime/output_fragmenter.cc)
SDKs: update node/python/sdk to understand sentinel events and to perform deterministic unescape before JSON parsing
Compat shim: server emits final 'X-Fragment-Manifest' event (compact JSON) when request includes header X-Redwood-Compat: legacy_manifest=true
Testing: add fuzz tests simulating truncation mid-fragment, retry loops with duplicate fragments, and nested tool-call boundaries
Canary: enable on internal 'canary-2' region with 5% traffic; collect structured-output decode metrics and choosen analytics
qa_steps: Run unit tests for sentinel parsing and escape/unescape logic across all SDKs
Run e2e with simulated 1-3% packet loss and random truncation points; verify client resumes and final JSON is correct
Verify tool/function-call idempotency: no duplicate external calls after retry for retried fragments already acked
Verify legacy_manifest compatibility: legacy SDK reconstructs final payload using manifest event with identical result
Manually validate Console shows fragment timeline and resume indicators for a sample request
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Models may emit literal sentinel-like text. Mitigation: deterministic escaping on server and SDK; prefix sentinel with non-printable control escape sequence when escaping active (configurable).
Risk: Increased stream size due to metadata. Mitigation: keep envelope minimal and use compact encoding; measure percent overhead in canary and cap if >2% token cost increase.
Risk: Older SDKs not adopting compat header. Mitigation: server will default to normal streaming for unknown clients; add analytics to identify clients and outreach via SDK updates and changelog.
Risk: Tool-call duplication on replay. Mitigation: idempotency tokens tied to frag_id and persisted short-term on gateway to suppress duplicates
